description: The Benzene Fenceline Monitoring Dashboard, run by the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), publishes the benzene concentrations that US petroleum refineries measure along their property boundaries under the 2015 Petroleum Refinery Sector Rule (40 CFR part 63 subpart CC, section 63.658). The dashboard page says refineries sample with passive tubes every two weeks, report quarterly (data public no later than about a month after each reporting deadline) and must run a root cause analysis and corrective action when the rolling annual average concentration difference exceeds the 9 micrograms per cubic metre action level; it warns that monitors also pick up benzene from neighbouring sources, roads, ports and wildfire smoke, and that the action level is not an ambient air standard. The dashboard is free to view online; separately, EPA's ScienceHub lists a 2019 analysis extract (analysis.csv and a data dictionary, updated 31 October 2024) with a paper by Mukerjee, Croghan and Smith. Coverage is all US refineries under the rule, from 2019. Caveats: bulk download options are not stated on the page read, and values reflect fenceline air, not stack emissions. For simulation it gives two-weekly fenceline benzene by refinery to spot upsets and releases and to compare with outages after hurricanes or floods. Related catalogue records include the EPA Toxics Release Inventory and the global refinery infrastructure data.
